pages.title: Tessel
pages.summary: Declarative server data for the browser: declare a query once, read it anywhere, and let the cache decide when to refetch.
pages.body:
Tessel keeps one cache of server data per app. Components declare which query they read, the cache hands back whatever it holds right away, and a refetch runs in the background only when the data has gone stale. There is no store to wire up and no loading state to thread through props.

## Install

<<sample:install>>

## Your first query

A query is a key plus a fetcher. Read it in any component and Tessel dedupes the request, shares the result, and keeps it fresh according to {sym:tessel/query#QueryOptions.staleTime}.

<<sample:hello>>

From here, the course walks through loading states, mutations, and server rendering in about an afternoon. If you already know what you want to do, the Do tab is task-shaped recipes and the Reference tab is every symbol with its contract per version.

pages.summary: Declare a piece of server data once; read it anywhere, and let the cache decide when to refetch.
pages.body:
## Minimal example

<<sample:minimal>>

## How freshness works

A query result is **fresh** until {sym:tessel/query#QueryOptions.staleTime} elapses. Fresh reads never hit the network. Stale reads return the cached value immediately and refetch in the background.

:::upgrade{from=v3.8 to=v4.0}
The default `staleTime` went from `0` to `30_000`.
:::

## Keys must be serializable

Every element of the key is compared by value, so it has to survive `JSON.stringify`. Passing a function or a class instance throws {sym:tessel/errors#QueryKeyError}.

pages.title: prefetch
pages.summary: Warm the cache for a query you're about to need, without subscribing to it.
pages.body:
## When to prefetch

Call {sym:tessel/query#prefetch} on hover or on route transition so the data is already in the cache when the screen mounts. It never subscribes, so nothing re-renders when the value changes.

pages.body:
1. Read the query as usual.
2. Check `query.isRefetching` to show a subtle indicator.
3. Do not gate rendering on `isLoading` after the first load.

pages.body: Call {sym:tessel/query#invalidate} from the mutation's success callback with the key prefix you wrote to.

pages.title: Prefetch on hover
pages.body: Attach {sym:tessel/query#prefetch} to `pointerenter` on the link that leads to the screen.

pages.title: Fresh, stale, and garbage-collected: the cache lifecycle
pages.summary: What happens to a result from the moment it arrives until it is dropped.
pages.body: A result is **fresh** for `staleTime`, then **stale** until it is read again, and it is **garbage-collected** once nothing has read it for `gcTime`.

pages.title: Why prefetch doesn't subscribe
pages.summary: Prefetching fills the cache; subscribing observes it.
pages.body: Subscribing would keep the result alive and trigger re-renders in components that never asked for it.

pages.summary: How the cache travels from server render to client hydration.
pages.body: Dehydrate the request-scoped cache after rendering and hydrate it before the first client read.

pages.title: Keep data fresh without refetching
pages.summary: Explain the difference between fresh and stale data, and choose a staleTime for a real screen instead of guessing.
pages.body:
:::card[You'll leave able to]
Explain the difference between fresh and stale data, and choose a `staleTime` for a real screen instead of guessing.
:::

In the workspace, clicking **Load profile** twice fetches the user twice. Nothing changed on the server in between, so the second request was wasted.

Tessel treats every result as **fresh** for a window of time. Inside that window, reads come straight from the cache. You set the window with {sym:tessel/query#QueryOptions.staleTime}.

Once that works, wait out the ten seconds and click again. The stale value appears instantly, and a background refetch replaces it. That's the next step.

changes.title: staleTime default: 0 → 30s
changes.why: In v3, every read of a mounted query could trigger a refetch. Most apps set staleTime by hand everywhere to stop it, so v4 picks a default that matches what people were already doing.

changes.title: QueryKey must be serializable
changes.why: Structural key comparison needs a stable serialization; functions and class instances silently produced cache misses.

changes.title: retry skips 4xx responses
changes.why: Retrying a request the server already rejected wastes time and can double-submit.

changes.title: useLegacyCache removed
changes.why: The v1 cache semantics were kept for two majors; nothing in the ecosystem still needed them.

changes.title: No refetch on window focus by default
changes.why: Focus refetches surprised more users than they helped; opt in per query.

changes.title: Errors keep last good data
changes.why: A failed refetch no longer clears the previous value, so screens degrade instead of blanking.

changes.title: prefetch resolves on cache hit
changes.why: Awaiting prefetch used to hang until the next network fetch even when the cache was fresh.

changes.title: invalidate(string) → invalidate(key)
changes.why: String prefixes could not express array keys; pass the same QueryKey you queried with.

changes.title: onSettled option
changes.why: Subscribe to the query instead; the callback ran outside the render lifecycle.

changes.title: signal option for cancellation
changes.why: Forward an AbortSignal so unmounting can cancel in-flight fetches.

changes.title: createServerClient
changes.why: A request-scoped client stops cache leaking between concurrent server renders.
